observations.finding: DMSO control (~80-100 cells/field, 1024x819px) shows spread adherent clusters with polygonal/spindle shapes. Treated fields show severe loss: f_a2646395beb5 = 3 detectable cell bodies, f_e1cfd248381b = 2 detectable cell bodies; >90% of field is empty black background at identical contrast. Few remaining cells are isolated, not in sheets.
Remaining treated cells are small, highly round with smooth, solid borders vs spread, protrusive control cells. No lamellipodia/filopodia visible in composite red/green.

Green: control = filamentous network throughout cytoplasm, moderate diffuse intensity. Treated = condensed bright small masses lacking spread filaments, high local intensity heterogeneity/contrast in the 1-3 round bodies.

Red (F-actin): control = prominent cortical red at cell periphery and intercellular contacts. Treated = minimal to absent red signal; at most faint thin red halo around green masses, no spread stress-fiber or cortical band detectable in composite colour alone.
Blue (DNA) inside green masses appears as small dense dot vs larger oval diffuse nuclei in control. Nuclei occupy larger fraction of small round cell body.

notable_cells.why: bright green butterfly-shaped condensed tubulin mass with two blue foci inside; exemplifies rounded, small, high-contrast tubulin phenotype with no red actin spread

candidate_mechanisms.why: Phenotype is strong rounding/shrinkage/solidification and tubulin condensation with cell loss (cell_roundness z=39.4 0.808 vs 0.562, solidity z=14.7 0.944 vs 0.85, eccentricity z=-32.2 0.556 vs 0.771, major_axis z=-12.3 65.9 vs 93.6, area z=-9.9 2419 vs 3839; tub_glcm_contrast z=34.0 0.012 vs 0.001, tub_std z=10.0 0.492 vs 0.147; nuc_area_ratio z=-15.2 2.63 vs 4.85). This is compatible with cytoskeletal/mitotic perturbagens (Actin disruptors, Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers, Aurora kinase inhibitors, Eg5 inhibitors) which all cause rounding, reduced spreading and cell detachment at 10uM, and red loss suggests actin disruption. With only composites, n=6 cells measured across 2 fields, no resolvable filament bundles vs depolymerization, no clear multinucleation/fragmentation, cannot distinguish between these listed MoAs; no single class is supported over others.

report.uncertainty: Composite-only, very low cell number (cells_measured=6) limits stain interpretation; identical contrast settings indicate changes are biological not imaging. No actin or cell-count features in top_deviations, so those observations set to agrees_with_measurements=false.

Beta-tubulin (green in composite, 1024x819 px): green microtubule network remains fibrous and present, extending into thin arborized processes in treated; no diffuse loss or dense bundling/collapse vs. DMSO. No tubulin metric provided to compare.

data.critique: Top call is plausible but not yet justified at p=0.62. At 1µM the Aurora-like signal is strong (frac_large_nucleus z=+61, 0.123 vs 0; frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+13, 0.515 vs 0.17; nuc_solidity z=-29.8; visual enlarged/lobed/multinucleate cells, e4/e7), and tubulin is not described as depolymerized/bundled. Most importantly the atlas (e9) contradicts Aurora: 0/10 Aurora neighbours, 5/10 Protein synthesis, 2/10 Eg5, top similarity 0.775 to Protein synthesis; assigning Protein synthesis only 0.08 is not calibrated. All key wells are single-replicate (rep 1 only); the 10µM well has only 6 cells and drives the monotonic roundness/tubulin trends, while frac_large_nucleus/multinucleation are non-monotonic and non-significant (rho=-0.40 p=0.6; rho=-0.20 p=0.8). data.note:
Reflection: Unblinded as mitoxantrone (CID4212, ChEMBL58) - identity check name and BBBC021 structure agree; ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor; DNA inhibitor, BBBC021 annotated as 'DNA replication' (e24).

Correct MoA is DNA replication class (topoisomerase II/DNA intercalator), not Microtubule destabilizers (p=0.34) or Aurora (initial p=0.62).

Phenotype misled: at 1.0µM we saw strong polyploid signature frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1 (0.123 vs 0), frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+13 (0.515 vs 0.17), nuc_solidity z=-29.8, with visual enlarged/lobed/multinucleate cells (e4/e7). This mimics Aurora mitotic failure but is also expected downstream of topo II inhibition/DNA damage-induced cytokinesis failure and cell-cycle arrest. Literature confirms mitoxantrone is an alkylaminoanthraquinone with topoisomerase II-dependent cytotoxicity (PMID 9054961) and review of DNA topoisomerase II as cancer target (PMID 42442624).

Atlas correctly contradicted Aurora: combined atlas 5/10 Protein synthesis, 2/10 Eg5, 0/10 Aurora (e9); isolated 1µM atlas 5/10 Microtubule destabilizers (top vincristine 0.782), 4/10 Protein synthesis, 0/10 Aurora, 0/10 DNA replication (e20). No DNA replication reference neighbours emerged, and we over-weighted visual polyploidy over orthogonal atlas evidence. Single-replicate wells and toxic 10µM well with n=6 cells further biased monotonic trends. In future, need DNA damage markers (γH2AX, p53) and DNA-content flow to distinguish topoisomerase-induced polyploidy from microtubule/Aurora phenotypes.

reflection.text:
After unblinding this is a clear miss on my part: truth is mitoxantrone - DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor / DNA inhibitor [e23,e24] consistent with PMID 42442624 and PMID 9054961 and PMID 32951576 - and I finished on Microtubule destabilizers p=0.34 after first concluding Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.62, while DNA replication was held at 0.01 throughout hypothesis history step 18 and step 21.

What the data did get right: the polyploidy phenotype was real and strong at the intermediate doses. acquire_well w_71aa1c3eef dose 5 1uM rep1 [e4] 46 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1, nuc_solidity z=-29.8, act_glcm_contrast z=+26.1. w_ef32b2e30b dose 6 3uM rep1 [e5] 52 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+35.0. w_da9f3d3374 dose 4 0.3uM rep1 [e3] 72 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+15.0, cell_roundness z=-12.2. describe_phenotype at 1uM [e7] and 0.3uM [e8] both noted density lower vs DMSO with enlarged/lobed/multinucleate cells and e7 explicitly listed Aurora candidates. That is compatible with topo II inhibition causing failed decatenation / endoreduplication, but it is morphologically indistinguishable from Aurora B cytokinesis failure without a mitosis-specific marker. I assigned it exclusively to Aurora and listed DNA replication as contradicting e4/e7, which was wrong.

What misled me:
1. Over-weighting subjective visual calls and ignoring atlas contradiction. The first compare_to_reference_atlas [e9] was 0/10 Aurora, 5/10 Protein synthesis (top similarity 0.775), 2/10 Eg5. Review correctly noted assigning Protein synthesis only 0.08 was not calibrated. The second atlas isolated to the 1uM well [e20] was 5/10 Microtubule destabilizers, 4/10 Protein synthesis, 1/10 Epithelial, still 0/10 Aurora. Instead of reconsidering DNA damage/replication, I simply downgraded Aurora 0.62->0.22 and upgraded the new atlas winner to 0.34 [e21,e22].
2. Driving dose-response trends with a toxic low-n well. Well w_8a03ddeae8 dose 7 10uM rep1 [e2] had only 6 cells measured but extreme z-scores cell_roundness +39.4, tub_glcm_contrast +34.1, cell_eccentricity -32.2. That single point created the monotonic Spearman rho=+1.00 p=0 for cell_roundness [e12] and tub_glcm_contrast [e16] which I cited as support for Aurora/Microtubule conclusions [e19,e22]. Meanwhile the relevant polyploidy trends were non-significant and non-monotonic: frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 [e10], frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.20 p=0.8 [e11], act_glcm_contrast rho=-0.40 p=0.6 [e13], act_std rho=-0.20 p=0.8 [e17], nuc_solidity rho=+0.40 p=0.6 [e15], cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 [e14] with n=4 wells. I treated noisy trends as confirmatory.
3. Acquisition choice. list_available_experiments [e1] showed 8 doses, 4 of 4 wells left. I used all budget on single-replicate wells at 0.3, 1, 3, 10uM [e2-e5], leaving 0 left and no replicates as noted in review. e6 at 10uM (density higher, unknown) conflicted with e2/e7/e8 (density lower) but I had no replicate to resolve. This left me unable to run the discriminating DNA-content / pHH3 / tubulin polymerization follow-up proposed in my own next_experiment.
4. No literature anchor for the phenocopy in this run. search_literature 'mitoxantrone topoisomerase II inhibitor DNA replication' returned hits [e25] but search_literature 'topoisomerase II inhibitor enlarged nuclei multinucleation polyploidy' returned 0 hits [e26]. With no PMID in this run directly linking topo II inhibition to large-nucleus/multinucleation, and without DNA replication markers in the panel, I defaulted to the cytoskeletal/mitotic kinase interpretation supported by act_glcm_contrast/act_std and stellate arborization notes at 0.3uM [e3,e8].

In retrospect the correct interpretation was that frac_large_nucleus +61 and multinucleation can occur via DNA replication/topoisomerase stress as well as Aurora B loss, and the atlas signal for Microtubule destabilizers/Protein synthesis reflects shared large-cell morphology, not mechanism. Replication, DNA-content flow cytometry, gamma-H2AX/EdU, and phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 were needed to distinguish, as review suggested.
what_was_right: Strong polyploidy signal at 1-3uM: e4 z=+61.1 frac_large_nucleus, z=-29.8 nuc_solidity, 0.515 vs 0.17 multinucleate; e5 z=+35.0; e7 visual enlarged/lobed/multinucleate
what_was_wrong: Held DNA replication/damage at 0.01 throughout despite matching phenotype; flipped to Microtubule destabilizers 0.34 based solely on e20 atlas 5/10 with 0 Aurora neighbours; trusted monotonic cell_roundness/tub_glcm rho=1.00 driven by n=6 toxic well e2

reflection.next_experiment: Re-run with replicates at 0.3,1,3 uM plus DNA replication controls: DNA content flow, EdU incorporation, gamma-H2AX, phospho-H3 Ser10, and tubulin polymerization assay vs vincristine/demecolcine and etoposide/mitoxantrone references to separate topoisomerase-mediated polyploidy from microtubule/Aurora cytokinesis failure.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Top call is plausible but not yet justified at p=0.62. At 1µM the Aurora-like signal is strong (frac_large_nucleus z=+61, 0.123 vs 0; frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+13, 0.515 vs 0.17; nuc_solidity z=-29.8; visual enlarged/lobed/multinucleate cells, e4/e7), and tubulin is not described as depolymerized/bundled. However the runner-ups are not excluded: actin disruption also explains act_glcm_contrast/act_std (z=+26/+22 at 1µM; z=+13/+10 at 0.3µM with stellate arborization, e3/e8) and can cause cytokinesis failure/binucleation. Most importantly the atlas (e9) contradicts Aurora: 0/10 Aurora neighbours, 5/10 Protein synthesis, 2/10 Eg5, top similarity 0.775 to Protein synthesis; assigning Protein synthesis only 0.08 is not calibrated. All key wells are single-replicate (rep 1 only); the 10µM well has only 6 cells and drives the monotonic roundness/tubulin trends, while frac_large_nucleus/multinucleation are non-monotonic and non-significant (rho=-0.40 p=0.6; rho=-0.20 p=0.8). Budget is exhausted (0 left), so no new well is affordable, but a free discriminating analysis remains.

Requested: Run compare_to_reference_atlas on only the already-acquired 1.0µM well w_71aa1c3eef (dose index 5, rep 1), excluding the toxic n=6 10µM well and the actin-like 0.3µM well. If Aurora neighbours emerge at this polyploid dose, approve Aurora; if Protein synthesis/Eg5 still dominate with no Aurora neighbours, downgrade Aurora and upgrade the atlas-supported runner-up.

## Reflection

After unblinding this is a clear miss on my part: truth is mitoxantrone - DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor / DNA inhibitor [e23,e24] consistent with PMID 42442624 and PMID 9054961 and PMID 32951576 - and I finished on Microtubule destabilizers p=0.34 after first concluding Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.62, while DNA replication was held at 0.01 throughout hypothesis history step 18 and step 21.

What the data did get right: the polyploidy phenotype was real and strong at the intermediate doses. acquire_well w_71aa1c3eef dose 5 1uM rep1 [e4] 46 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1, nuc_solidity z=-29.8, act_glcm_contrast z=+26.1. w_ef32b2e30b dose 6 3uM rep1 [e5] 52 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+35.0. w_da9f3d3374 dose 4 0.3uM rep1 [e3] 72 cells: frac_large_nucleus z=+15.0, cell_roundness z=-12.2. describe_phenotype at 1uM [e7] and 0.3uM [e8] both noted density lower vs DMSO with enlarged/lobed/multinucleate cells and e7 explicitly listed Aurora candidates. That is compatible with topo II inhibition causing failed decatenation / endoreduplication, but it is morphologically indistinguishable from Aurora B cytokinesis failure without a mitosis-specific marker. I assigned it exclusively to Aurora and listed DNA replication as contradicting e4/e7, which was wrong.

What misled me:
1. Over-weighting subjective visual calls and ignoring atlas contradiction. The first compare_to_reference_atlas [e9] was 0/10 Aurora, 5/10 Protein synthesis (top similarity 0.775), 2/10 Eg5. Review correctly noted assigning Protein synthesis only 0.08 was not calibrated. The second atlas isolated to the 1uM well [e20] was 5/10 Microtubule destabilizers, 4/10 Protein synthesis, 1/10 Epithelial, still 0/10 Aurora. Instead of reconsidering DNA damage/replication, I simply downgraded Aurora 0.62->0.22 and upgraded the new atlas winner to 0.34 [e21,e22].
2. Driving dose-response trends with a toxic low-n well. Well w_8a03ddeae8 dose 7 10uM rep1 [e2] had only 6 cells measured but extreme z-scores cell_roundness +39.4, tub_glcm_contrast +34.1, cell_eccentricity -32.2. That single point created the monotonic Spearman rho=+1.00 p=0 for cell_roundness [e12] and tub_glcm_contrast [e16] which I cited as support for Aurora/Microtubule conclusions [e19,e22]. Meanwhile the relevant polyploidy trends were non-significant and non-monotonic: frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.40 p=0.6 [e10], frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.20 p=0.8 [e11], act_glcm_contrast rho=-0.40 p=0.6 [e13], act_std rho=-0.20 p=0.8 [e17], nuc_solidity rho=+0.40 p=0.6 [e15], cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 [e14] with n=4 wells. I treated noisy trends as confirmatory.
3. Acquisition choice. list_available_experiments [e1] showed 8 doses, 4 of 4 wells left. I used all budget on single-replicate wells at 0.3, 1, 3, 10uM [e2-e5], leaving 0 left and no replicates as noted in review. e6 at 10uM (density higher, unknown) conflicted with e2/e7/e8 (density lower) but I had no replicate to resolve. This left me unable to run the discriminating DNA-content / pHH3 / tubulin polymerization follow-up proposed in my own next_experiment.
4. No literature anchor for the phenocopy in this run. search_literature 'mitoxantrone topoisomerase II inhibitor DNA replication' returned hits [e25] but search_literature 'topoisomerase II inhibitor enlarged nuclei multinucleation polyploidy' returned 0 hits [e26]. With no PMID in this run directly linking topo II inhibition to large-nucleus/multinucleation, and without DNA replication markers in the panel, I defaulted to the cytoskeletal/mitotic kinase interpretation supported by act_glcm_contrast/act_std and stellate arborization notes at 0.3uM [e3,e8].

In retrospect the correct interpretation was that frac_large_nucleus +61 and multinucleation can occur via DNA replication/topoisomerase stress as well as Aurora B loss, and the atlas signal for Microtubule destabilizers/Protein synthesis reflects shared large-cell morphology, not mechanism. Replication, DNA-content flow cytometry, gamma-H2AX/EdU, and phospho-Histone H3 Ser10 were needed to distinguish, as review suggested.

What was right:
- Strong polyploidy signal at 1-3uM: e4 z=+61.1 frac_large_nucleus, z=-29.8 nuc_solidity, 0.515 vs 0.17 multinucleate; e5 z=+35.0; e7 visual enlarged/lobed/multinucleate

What was wrong or missed:
- Held DNA replication/damage at 0.01 throughout despite matching phenotype; flipped to Microtubule destabilizers 0.34 based solely on e20 atlas 5/10 with 0 Aurora neighbours; trusted monotonic cell_roundness/tub_glcm rho=1.00 driven by n=6 toxic well e2

Proposed next experiment: Re-run with replicates at 0.3,1,3 uM plus DNA replication controls: DNA content flow, EdU incorporation, gamma-H2AX, phospho-H3 Ser10, and tubulin polymerization assay vs vincristine/demecolcine and etoposide/mitoxantrone references to separate topoisomerase-mediated polyploidy from microtubule/Aurora cytokinesis failure.
